# Welcome

This course offers hands-on training in simulating, operating, and optimizing
thermal power plants using KONGSBERG's K-Sim Connect cloud-based digital platform.

**Instructors:** Dr. Sanja Boskovic & Serhat Beyenir

# Course Highlights

The K-Sim Engine Thermal Power Plant simulator is based on a real thermal power
plant in Västerås, Sweden. It trains and assesses plant operators in start-up,
optimization, shutdown, emergency situations, and safety procedures.

- High-fidelity generic model replicating real power plant behaviour
- Real-time simulation of boilers, turbines, feedwater systems, and control loops
- Rankine cycle and district heat system simulation
- Plant performance analysis and optimization
- Efficiency and environmental impact assessment

# Lectures and Labs

Each topic pairs a lecture with a hands-on simulator lab. Students collect
real operating data from the K-Sim platform and analyse it using Python.

| # | Topic | Key Calculations |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Boiler Efficiency | Direct method, Dulong formula, LHV |
| 2 | Turbine Efficiency | Isentropic efficiency, steam quality |
| 3 | Power Plant Efficiency | Overall cycle efficiency, heat rate |
| 4 | NOx Emissions | Emission factors, regulatory limits |
| 5 | Heat Exchangers | LMTD, effectiveness, fouling |
| 6 | Combustion Analysis | Stoichiometry, excess air, flue gas |

# Computing

Simulation scripts are written in Python using industry-standard libraries:

- [`iapws`](https://iapws.readthedocs.io/) — IAPWS-IF97 steam tables
- [`numpy`](https://numpy.org/) — numerical computation
- [`matplotlib`](https://matplotlib.org/) — plotting and visualization
- [`scipy`](https://scipy.org/) — engineering calculations

The course environment is managed with [`uv`](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv).
Code quality is maintained with [`ruff`](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/) and
[`black`](https://black.readthedocs.io/).
